title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1968-08-21

ai_review.summary: High‑energy August 21 1968 Fillmore West show captured on a solid soundboard source – crisp Pigpen vocals and killer Dark Star/Alligator suites despite a rough opening track.
ai_review.review: The performance is a quintessential 1968 set, mixing Anthem of the Sun material with the emerging Live Dead repertoire. Reviewers rave about the extended Dark Star → Other One → Cryptical suite, the fiery Alligator jam and Pigpen’s powerful vocals on Good Morning Little School Girl and Midnight Hour. The recording is a 4‑generation soundboard tape – overall clear and well‑balanced, though the first track sounds “awful” from the cassette source and Lovelight ends abruptly.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of detailed reviews are glowing (average 4.7★) and highlight both an exceptional musical performance and a generally good soundboard recording, with only minor technical flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: 4th‑gen SBD derived from a cassette off‑reel master – first track muffly/awful, later tracks crisp and well balanced. Some duplication of “Good Morning Little School Girl” and an abrupt cut‑off at the end of Love Light are noted.

show_quality.setlist_flow: A high‑energy 1968 set that blends Anthem of the Sun material with the newer Live Dead songs; suites are kept together for seamless transitions, creating a flowing psychedelic journey.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for fiery guitar tone, mountain‑jam theme in Alligator, Goodnight motif, strong vocal on Death Don't Have No Mercy, and early country twang on Midnight Hour; low vocal volume noted only during Cryptical reprise.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for intertwining bass lines with Jerry’s lead, creating a “psychic dance” during Dark Star and other jams.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen lauded for powerful organ/harmonica work, stellar vocals on Alligator, Good Morning Little School Girl, and Midnight Hour; organ mic’d well throughout.
band_member_comments.Drums: Double‑drummer feel noted on Midnight Hour; drums heat up before Alligator and drive the high‑energy sections.
